newsitem.title: USA: NHTSA cites low Chrysler latch replacement response.
newsitem.headline: NHTSA cites low Chrysler latch replacement response.

text.p: Federal safety officials Thursday expressed concern that many owners of older Chrysler minivans were not heeding recommendations that stronger, safer rear liftgate latches be installed on the vehicles.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said that the repair campaign to put new latches on the 1984 through 1995 model minivans was making good progress, but the response rate for the older models was low.
At the agency's insistence, Chrysler last year agreed to replace the latches, which could open in a low-speed crash, although the automaker denied that they were a safety problem.
The replacement programme covers about 4 million Plymouth Voyager, Dodge Caravan and Chrysler Town and Country vans.

NHTSA Administrator Ricardo Martinez said the installation completion rate for 1993-1995 models was about 60 percent, but that fell to 26 percent for 1984-1989 model year vans without a remote release switch and 14 percent for 1984-l989 models with the remote release.

"Automobile safety on our roads is our highest priority and we strongly urge minivan owners to obtain the stronger, safer rear latch from their dealers as soon as possible," Martinez said in a statement.
